newsitem.title: USA: Wendy's says April sales up, sees margins up.
newsitem.headline: Wendy's says April sales up, sees margins up.

text.p: Wendy's International Inc said its U.S. restaurant sales rose 11.1 percent in April, compared with a decline of 0.5 percent in the same period last year, company executives said Tuesday.
The executives, in an interview with Reuters, also said Wendy's operating margins continue to improve.

"We're satisified we can keep the momentum on margins going from the first quarter," said Frederick Reed, Wendy's chief financial officer. "We definitely expect improvements against the second quarter of last year."
Reed said it was "still too early" to give specific figures.
The company had margins of 14.5 percent in its second quarter of 1996. In the first quarter, it had margins of 13.0 percent, compared with 11.1 percent in last year's first quarter.
Gordon Teter, Wendy's chairman, president and chief executive, said the improved sales and margins stemmed from the continued "quality" of Wendy's food offerings.
They also came, he said, amid a much-publicized promotion from rival McDonald's Corp, which last month slashed the price of a Big Mac to $0.55 with the purchase of fries and a soft drink.
"Unlike some of our competitors, we have not made our food products into commodities," Teter said.
Teter and Reed were in New York to promote Wendy's fresh-stuffed pitas. Tomorrow, they will ring the opening bell at the New York Stock Exchange and distribute pitas to traders.

Wendy's has more than 5,000 restaurants worldwide, although only 600 outside the U.S. The company "easily" expects to more than double its international locations by the turn of the century, Teter said. Latin America and the far East are likely areas of expansion, he added.
Wendy's also owns about 1,300 Tim Hortons, a Canadian breakfast chain it bought in 1995. The company expects to add more than $850 million in revenues from Tim Hortons in 1997, Teter said.
It will open 270 new Tim Hortons for the year, with about 100 of those opening in the U.S., he added.
